$comment: Configuration: vendors define subscription labels, windows and model tiers; roles list tier preferences; thresholds are percent used and reset grace minutes. last_verified is an ISO date. Refresh with /audit-orchestrator.

frontier.note: Fable 5.1: deepest reasoning; has its own weekly cap. Use for planning/architecture/hard debugging only.

strong.note: Opus 5.5: Anthropic's recommended default; the everyday writer. Clean, maintainable code. Default coder. Default effort medium; we run high for implementation.

mid.note: Sonnet 5.5: reviews, verification, research, test writing.

cheap.note: Haiku 5.5 (2026-10-07): exploration, titles, summaries, mechanical edits. Falls back to claude-haiku-4-5-20250101 if the alias is gated.

anthropic.fable_note: On plans that include Fable, Fable draws from the weekly pool under its own scoped limit ('weekly_scoped' in the usage endpoint). Routing treats that window separately.

frontier.note: GPT-6 Astra: frontier tier (API $10/$50). Planning/hard debugging when Fable/Claude is constrained. Expensive in subscription usage terms; use sparingly.

strong.note: GPT-6.1 Sol: Codex's workhorse (500k ctx in Codex, 'near-Astra at 1/5 cost'). Long-running autonomous implementation and blind second-opinion review.

mid.note: Same model, medium effort: code review of Anthropic-written code (cross-vendor review).

cheap.note: GPT-6 Luna (API $0.10/$0.50): exploration, lint-level review, summaries. ~10x cheaper in usage than Sol.

openai.notes: GPT-5.5/5.4 retired from ChatGPT sign-in (Oct 2026). 'ultra' effort auto-delegates subagents inside Codex. Fast tier costs 2.5x usage; never enable it automatically.
openai.catalog_note: Verify the live catalog for your account with `codex debug models`; the audit skill does this.

planner.purpose: Deep, tireless, meticulous planning and architecture. Thinks; does not write product code.

coder.purpose: Writes the actual code. Clean, maintainable, beautiful.

reviewer.purpose: Reviews code written by the OTHER vendor (cross-vendor review). Correctness + craft.

verifier.purpose: Runs tests, reproduces bugs, checks claims against reality, red-team QA.

researcher.purpose: Reads docs and the web, summarizes with citations.

thresholds.$comment: percent used. A window that resets within soon_minutes is treated one level greener because it will clear before a long task finishes.

effort_policy.$comment: Effort scales with the task, never pinned. Sizes: trivial (rename, one-liner), small (<1h, one file), medium (one bounded brief), large (multi-file slice), hard (gnarly bug, architecture, subtle concurrency). Default size is medium. Escalate on failure, not pre-emptively. Both vendors use low|medium|high|xhigh|max; Claude maps max->max, OpenAI additionally has ultra (never automatic).

conductor.$comment: Which front door owns a project by default and how hand-back works. Flips happen only when the active conductor's own vendor is red (forced) or, for the away conductor, at a brief boundary once the home vendor is stably green again.

runtime.$comment: Wrap detached workers and the supervisor in caffeinate (macOS) / systemd-inhibit (Linux) so long runs survive idle sleep. Lid-closed sleep still happens on a laptop without external display + power.
